_readme: Registry of pages that DESCRIBE how the site works. Each entry pins the code whose behaviour the prose asserts; when that code changes, `npm run validate` flags the page for re-review and prints its claims[] as a checklist. Stamp only AFTER actually re-reading the page: `node scripts/doc-provenance.js --stamp --doc <page>`. Rationale + the stable-prose/generated-evidence rule: _personal/ARTICLE-WRITER-SPEC.md. Origin: articles/methodology.html described a verification process that had already changed, and nothing caught it.
_not_registered: Normative rulebooks (docs/BOTH-SIDES.md, docs/QA-AUDIT-RUBRIC.md, CLAUDE.md) are deliberately absent. They DEFINE required behaviour rather than describe existing behaviour -- code drifting from them is a code bug, not a doc bug, and the QA gates already enforce that direction.

claims: The 'How the analysis is produced' paragraph matches the real pipeline.

The verification description matches what the ledgers actually RECORD. Bill ledgers record an auditing model and NO drafting model (0 of 212 as of 2026-08-30), so no page may claim of a BILL analysis that a different model audited what drafted it. The cross-model rule is enforced only in the ARTICLE lane, by publish-article.js.
Ownership, funding, and independence statements are still accurate.
The named editor matches data/entity.json.
The static-data claim still holds: api.js fetches only same-host JSON, and the browser makes no live government API call.
The quote counts (468 / 430 with a granule id / 417 bill-page / 0 with a granule id / 432 with a bill id) are derived -- re-run `node scripts/generate-site-facts.js --check` before stamping.
The page must NOT claim a granule identifier on every quote, nor that any of them is rendered as a link -- no front-end file reads the field.

The verbatim promise is scoped to MEMBER QUOTES. Tracker positions are sourced to the holder's published document, which can be a press release; data/ref-sources.json registers one. A sitewide "we do not quote press releases" is false.
The speaker-resolution description must match resolveRepInfo, including that it takes the first remaining candidate when more than one still matches.
The excerpt description must match bestExcerpt in every branch, including the trim-to-last-word fallback.

The member-profile count, the role split, the seats-with-two-profiles figure and the roll-call/voice-vote counts are all derived -- re-run `node scripts/generate-site-facts.js --check` before stamping.
The Senate matching description must match lib/senator-match.js, including that an ambiguous row is left UNMATCHED rather than guessed.
The page must NOT claim member records store term data -- no such field exists in the schema.

The crossover description must keep the tie carve-out: a party that splits exactly even has no majority direction, so nobody in it is listed. A tie silently defaulting to Yea put a named senator on the public crossover list 18 times before 2026-08-30.
Any on-page label the prose names must be the exact string the renderer emits -- it is "Crossed the Aisle", not "Crossovers".

The claim about what the browser loads must stay narrow: member portraits load from bioguide.congress.gov (util.js portraitUrl) and app-settings.js calls two geolocation APIs, so "everything is static and same-host" is false.
The schema.org types this page names are the types actually emitted. Verify against generate_bill_pages.js and lib/entity.js -- do NOT trust the prose.
Bill pages emit Legislation (not LegislativeAction). Articles use LegislativeAction only inside their about field.
Any schema type claimed here must exist somewhere in the codebase. Quotation and rep-profile Person schema were claimed but NOT implemented (caught 2026-08-13).
The canonical Person / NewsMediaOrganization entity-reference architecture is still in place.
The described bill-text version rule matches the fetch logic (newest applicable: Enrolled > Engrossed > Reported > Introduced).
The described sourcing workflow matches the workflow actually run.
The list of validation gates matches what validate-batch.js actually enforces.
The latest-applicable-version fetch rule is still how bill text is retrieved.
Any count or enumeration on this page (number of checks, number of passes) still matches reality -- these are the parts that rot first.
The neutrality rules described here match the rules the drafting prompt actually enforces.
The both-sides eligibility triggers described match docs/BOTH-SIDES.md.
The stated ban on editorial labels is still enforced in the prompt.
The quote counts and the "no session field anywhere" claim are derived -- re-run `node scripts/generate-site-facts.js --check` before stamping.
The page must NOT claim the site notes the date and session of each quote, nor that bill-page quotes carry a granule id: 0 of 417 do, and no record in either store has a session field.

The bill-page extractor also pulls minority/additional/dissenting views from committee reports, a different GovInfo collection from the Congressional Record -- the page must not describe that store as Record-only.
Claims about the Record itself must trace to the stored CRS 98-265 or the stored GovInfo help page, including the Senate unanimous-consent carve-out (undelivered Senate remarks printed as if spoken).

Every count on this page is derived: re-run `node scripts/generate-site-facts.js --check` before stamping. The bill total, the signed total, the top-line and summary distributions and the skip-list breakdown all come from that sheet.

The coverage sentence must NOT claim the site tracks all legislation with floor action -- data/analysis-skip.json deliberately excludes CRA disapproval resolutions, which reach the floor by design. That overclaim was live from May to 2026-08-30.

The bill-text paragraph must keep disclosing the version lag. The pipeline prefers the newest applicable version at FETCH time; an already-cached bill that advances is not re-fetched, so the stored text can be older than what Congress.gov lists.
The bill-text panel label rendered by bill.js is still "Full Bill Text" -- the page must not call it the enrolled bill.
The 30% crossover threshold still matches fetch_vote_data.js.
The bio's description of the verification pipeline is still accurate.
The 'How this work is produced' section matches editorial-standards.html.
The page is regenerated (npm run author) rather than hand-edited -- hand edits will be overwritten.
Nothing published comes from an AI model's background knowledge; every figure/date/citation must appear in fetched source text.
A facts sheet with line numbers is extracted, and published figures are copied from it rather than retyped.
Referenced statutes are fetched and read when a bill amends another law.

The blocking/warning split is stated accurately: the section counts in validate-batch.js still match the page (27 sections, 14 that can call fail(), 13 warn-only), and the figure-sourcing guard is still warn-only outside --strict. Re-derive with `node scripts/generate-site-facts.js --check`.
QA re-reads happen in fresh sessions carrying no memory of prior passes, working adversarially.
Drafts are decomposed into atomic claims judged supported / contradicted / unsupported against a quoted span, including a direction-of-change check.

The cross-model rule is stated ONLY where it is enforced. publish-article.js blocks an ARTICLE whose ledger names the same model family as drafter and auditor; bill ledgers record no drafting model, so the page must not claim it for bill analyses.
A per-page audit ledger records every claim, its verdict, and its source line.

CRITICAL -- every analysis and article is reviewed by a human BEFORE publication. If the Dispatch lane ever auto-publishes with post-publish review, this page AND the disclosure line on every article become false and must be reworded first.

Quotations are never generated or paraphrased; verbatim from the Congressional Record with speaker attribution, or omitted. The page must NOT claim a date on every quote — only 23 of 417 bill-attached quotes store one (checked 2026-08-30).
Positions attributed to named organizations trace to a fetched primary source, or are omitted rather than softened.
No AI-generated or AI-altered imagery is used.
